precepts.why:
Leviticus 12:4 says “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.” Purification means being washed, cleansed, made holy; literally, removing what is foreign and contaminated to restore something to its natural clean state. So purification is not just staying away from the temple. The days of her separation are also her being nursed back to health, restored.

Esther shows purification too. Go there and read it for yourselves: Esther went through her days of purification with sweet odours and so forth, and everything else she needed, and she had maids to help her. It is a different purification, but it shows that purifying a woman is a lot of stuff: care, help, the right food, the things her body needs.

So it is with a woman after she gives birth. She was not just sent home and left alone. For those forty days, or eighty for a girl, she was kept in a special place, and midwives and family came, cooked the right food and nursed her back to health. That is postpartum in the Bible, and it is why a sister who has just given birth needs people around her and help with the baby, not the postpartum depression that Esau made up.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
The law shows what conceiving is: “Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days”. She conceived what? Seed.

A woman conceives seed through intercourse. That is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground in Genesis 38, knowing the inheritance would not be his. It is the same exact thing.

So Luke 1:31, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”, is a woman conceiving seed and bearing a man child. It is said to Mary in the same form of words as to Zacharias about Elisabeth: “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John,” and “shalt call his name JESUS.” The same thing being done, the same thing being said.

precepts.why:
In Acts 15 certain men came down from Judea and taught, “Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” Why does it say after the manner of Moses and not just circumcision? Leviticus 12 shows the manner of Moses. A woman who “conceived seed, and born a man child” is unclean seven days; “in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised”; she continues in the blood of her purifying thirty-three more days, forty in all for a boy and eighty for a girl. When the days are fulfilled she brings a lamb and a pigeon or turtledove for a burnt offering and a sin offering, and if she cannot afford a lamb, “two turtles, or two young pigeons”. The priest makes the atonement, and the offering covers the child as well as the mother.

Luke 2 confirms it with Mary and Christ. Mary conceived seed and bore a man child. “And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” That is the eighth day of Leviticus 12.

“And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord”, because “Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”. Then comes the offering: “to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.” Those are the offerings Leviticus 12:8 names.

So behind circumcision after the manner of Moses comes sacrifice. It is circumcision with the eighth day, the days of purifying and the offering for the woman and the child all tied together. That is what the men from Judea were pressing on the Gentiles, and that is why the scripture calls it the manner of Moses.

precepts.text: Moses gave unto you circumcision, not because it is of Moses but of the fathers: Abraham's circumcision is not the manner of Moses.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
If circumcision after the manner of Moses is circumcision with sacrifice, is all circumcision of Moses? Christ answers it: “Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.”

Moses gave it to them, but circumcision is not of Moses. It is of the fathers, of Abraham, who was the one first circumcised. So when Acts 15 says circumcised after the manner of Moses, that is not the same thing as the circumcision of Abraham.

There are two different things here: circumcision of the fathers, and circumcision after the manner of Moses with the sacrifice of Leviticus 12 behind it. Seeing that difference is what opens up what the Pharisees were demanding and what Paul was fighting in his letters.

precepts.text: Abraham was ninety-nine and Ishmael thirteen when circumcised: not the eighth day and no sacrifice, so not after the manner of Moses.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” “And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.”

Abraham was not circumcised on the eighth day after he was born; he was ninety-nine. Ishmael was thirteen. There was no eighth day, no days of purifying and no sacrifice. That is circumcision of the fathers, not circumcision after the manner of Moses.

The Pharisees wanted circumcision and sacrifice together, after the manner of Moses, because sacrificing was their bread and butter. As more people followed Christ, more of them stopped sacrificing, and if the people stop sacrificing, the Pharisees cannot eat. So they went into the churches saying you have to be circumcised to be saved. That is not what the Bible, Christ or the apostles taught. They were trying to put back on the people the yoke that could not be borne, the same one Peter asked about: “why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?”

precepts.text: Abraham circumcised Isaac at eight days as God commanded, before Moses and with no sacrifice; the Pharisees wanted circumcision with sacrifice because that was their bread and butter, and the more people followed Christ the less they sacrificed.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said”, and “Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.” Sarah conceived in old age and Abraham named the child Isaac. Then: “And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.” “And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.”

Isaac was circumcised on the eighth day, as God commanded, but this was long before Moses. There is no reading of them going and sacrificing animals for it. So even eighth-day circumcision here is not after the manner of Moses. There is circumcision of the fathers, and there is circumcision after the manner of Moses, which carries the sacrifice.

That is how Paul can say in Galatians 5, “if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.” He means circumcised after the manner of Moses, back under the yoke of bondage, taught by the Pharisees that you must be circumcised and sacrifice an animal to be saved. “For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.” Once the temple was destroyed and the priests scattered, that man had no way to keep it and was finished.

“Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.” Christ's sacrifice does away with the animal sacrifice, so whoever runs back to animals to atone for sin rejects what Christ did on the cross. Paul is not throwing out the commandments. He is rejecting the sacrifice that was bewitching the Galatians. So “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.”

precepts.text: In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised; the law Moses himself later carried to Israel.
precepts.point: This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.” This is the law Moses himself later carried to Israel, the same eighth day given to Abraham in Genesis 17.

The man who would carry that law had not kept the covenant with his own son, and the Lord met him by the way in the inn and sought to kill him. Zipporah's sharp stone and her word, “Surely a bloody husband art thou to me”, are what stood between Moses and death.

precepts.text: If she be not able to bring a lamb, she shall bring two turtles or two young pigeons; the offering of fowls served her purifying.
precepts.point: The third category is the burnt sacrifice of fowls, meaning birds: turtledoves or young pigeons. That is the offering meant when a woman after childbirth brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons, as in Leviticus 12.

note.label: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings

precepts.why:
The third category of burnt sacrifice is of fowls, meaning birds: “turtledoves, or of young pigeons.” This is the offering meant in Leviticus 12 for a woman after childbirth: “And if she be not able to bring a lamb, then she shall bring two turtles, or two young pigeons; the one for the burnt offering, and the other for a sin offering: and the priest shall make an atonement for her, and she shall be clean.”

The offering of fowls served her purifying. If she could not bring a lamb, two turtles or two young pigeons were brought, one of them the burnt offering of fowls laid out here, and the priest made an atonement for her.

precepts.text: If a woman have an issue of blood she shall be put apart seven days; those are the days of the separation.
precepts.point: The seven days match the law of the woman's issue: when her issue is blood, she is put apart seven days; those are the days of her separation spoken of here.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
When a woman has conceived seed and born a man child, “she shall be unclean seven days; according to the days of the separation for her infirmity shall she be unclean.” The seven days come from the law of the woman’s issue.

“And if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.” Those seven days she is put apart are the days of her separation, and the law of childbirth is measured by them: after a son, she is unclean the same seven days, as in her separation.

precepts.text: Every man child eight days old shall be circumcised, an everlasting covenant in the flesh; the uncircumcised is cut off.
precepts.point: That did not change. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John the Baptist, and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
“in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.” The law behind it is the covenant given to Abraham: “Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.”

The day is set there too: “he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations.” And it is not for a season: “my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.”

The penalty is plain: “the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.” That is why brothers coming into the truth must be circumcised.

precepts.text: On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and he was called John; John the Baptist was circumcised.
precepts.point: That did not change. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John the Baptist, and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
The eighth day did not change. “on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father. And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.”

John the Baptist was circumcised on the eighth day, exactly as Leviticus 12:3 and the covenant of Genesis 17 require. The law was still being kept in the days right before Christ.

precepts.text: When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus; Christ kept the same law.
precepts.point: That did not change. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John the Baptist, and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
“And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.”

Christ himself kept the same law. He was circumcised when the eight days were accomplished, the eighth day of Leviticus 12:3, and he was named at that time with the name the angel gave before he was conceived.

John the Baptist on the eighth day, and Christ on the eighth day: the law of circumcision did not change, and it stands for us.

precepts.text: When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished; Mary kept the law of the forty days.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
After a male child the mother is unclean forty days: seven days of separation plus “three and thirty days” of purifying. In all that time “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.”

Mary is the fulfilment of that: “when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord.” Mary had to do this law. She waited out the forty days, and only then came to the sanctuary with the child.

precepts.text: No king had any other beginning of birth; every man is fashioned to be flesh in ten months of the seed of man.
precepts.point: There is no king that had any other beginning of birth, and all men have one entrance into life. Christ was no exception: he was made of the seed of David according to the flesh, so it took seed to come through David's line.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
For a maid child the mother is “unclean two weeks, as in her separation”, and continues in the blood of her purifying “threescore and six days”: fourteen days plus sixty six days, eighty days for a daughter.

Solomon describes the birth every man has. “I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth, And in my mother’s womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man.” A full term pregnancy is forty weeks, which is ten months; they say nine months but forget the month of conception. He was compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and when he was born he drew in the common air and cried as all others do.

“For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth. For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out.” Every man, king or not, comes the same way, fashioned in his mother’s womb of seed; and the law of Leviticus 12 is written for the mothers who bear them.

precepts.text: Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.
precepts.point: There is no king that had any other beginning of birth, and all men have one entrance into life. Christ was no exception: he was made of the seed of David according to the flesh, so it took seed to come through David's line.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
There is no king that had any other beginning of birth, and Christ was no exception. He is “Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.”

Made of the seed of David: it took seed to come through David’s line. Christ was fashioned to be flesh in his mother’s womb like all men, and Mary bore him under the very law of purification laid out in Leviticus 12.

precepts.text: On the eighth day the flesh of a man child's foreskin shall be circumcised, made a law in Israel confirming Abraham's seal.
precepts.point: To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations.
